title: Is VAR making football fairer?
description: Explore whether VAR has improved fairness and decision-making in football, and its impact on the spectator experience...
question: Evaluate whether VAR has had a positive impact on professional football. Consider players, officials and spectators.

title: Would You Watch the ‘Steroid Olympics’?
subtopic: Ethics and deviance — Drugs and doping
description: What happens when performance-enhancing drugs are allowed in elite sport? The Enhanced Games challenge traditional ideas about fair competition, athlete welfare and sporting ethics. Explore why athletes might choose to use banned substances, the financial pressures behind their decisions and whether allowing doping could change the future of competitive sport.
question: What happens when performance-enhancing drugs are allowed in elite sport? The Enhanced Games challenge traditional ideas about fair competition, athlete welfare and sporting ethics. Explore why athletes might choose to use banned substances, the financial pressures behind their decisions and whether allowing doping could change the future of competitive sport.

title: VAR: Making Football Fairer or Creating More Controversy?
description: VAR was introduced to make football fairer, but is it actually working? BBC Sport investigates refereeing mistakes during the 2025–26 Premier League season, revealing which clubs benefited and suffered most. Explore how technology influences decision-making, the accountability of officials and spectators’ enjoyment of sport, linking directly to the advantages and disadvantages of modern technology.
question: Evaluate the extent to which VAR has improved fairness in professional football, considering the accuracy of decisions, pressure on officials and the impact on spectators. Use examples from the article to support your judgement.

title: Who Makes the Rules? FIFA Under Fire Over World Cup Decision
subtopic: Ethics and deviance — Sportsmanship and gamesmanship
description: When FIFA decided not to enforce a World Cup suspension following Folarin Balogun's red card, UEFA questioned the integrity of the decision. Explore how governing bodies influence fairness in elite sport and consider the importance of consistent rules, accountability and ethical decision-making in maintaining public confidence in international competitions
question: Evaluate the extent to which decisions made by international governing bodies can undermine fairness and integrity in sport. Use the FIFA controversy and other sporting examples to support your judgement.

title: When the Manager Loses It: Is Anger Effective Leadership?
description: After a disappointing first half against West Ham, Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta delivers an emotional team talk to his players. Explore how his communication and behaviour demonstrate characteristics of autocratic leadership. Consider how this approach might influence motivation, confidence and performance, and whether a different leadership style could be more effective.
question: Analyse the effectiveness of Arteta's leadership style during his half-time team talk. Under what circumstances might an autocratic approach be more effective than a democratic approach?

title: Can Training at Altitude Really Make You Faster?
description: The 1968 Mexico City Olympics changed how scientists understood altitude and athletic performance. Discover why reduced oxygen availability affected endurance runners differently from sprinters and how this led to the development of altitude training. Explore why endurance athletes now train at altitude to improve their performance when competing at sea level.
question: Evaluate the effectiveness of altitude training as a method of improving performance in endurance athletes. Consider both physiological benefits and potential limitations.

title: Can You Train Your Body to Beat the Heat?
subtopic: 1.1.d Environmental effects on body systems — Exercise in the heat
description: Could training in extreme heat help endurance athletes perform better? Researchers compared runners completing four weeks of heat acclimation with those training in normal conditions. Discover how exercise in hot environments affects body temperature, aerobic performance and energy use, and explore the physiological adaptations that may help athletes cope with competing in the heat.
question: Analyse how exercising in hot conditions affects temperature regulation and cardiovascular function, and evaluate how heat acclimation could influence endurance performance.

title: The Science Behind the Perfect Pole Vault
subtopic: 1.3.a Biomechanical principles, levers and the use of technology — Analysing movement through the use of technology
description: Can technology help an Olympic champion jump even higher? Discover how researchers used 28 high-speed cameras to analyse elite athletes at the World Indoor Championships. Olympic pole vaulter Katerina Stefanidi explains how biomechanical data revealed differences in her technique, helping coaches understand how small changes in movement can influence performance.
question: Analyse how biomechanical technology can be used to identify weaknesses in a pole vaulter's technique and improve sporting performance.

title: Can Virtual Reality Make You a Better Footballer?
subtopic: Types and methods of practice; transfer of skills
description: Could virtual reality help footballers make better decisions on the pitch? This research review examines 20 studies exploring how simulated sporting situations can develop decision-making skills in team sports. Discover how VR allows athletes to practise recognising situations and selecting appropriate responses, and consider whether these skills transfer into real competitive performance.
question: Evaluate the effectiveness of virtual reality training in developing decision-making skills in football. Consider how different methods of practice and positive or negative transfer might influence performance in real matches.
